methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: A guest column highlighting small-business AI adoption as the real challenge signals that infrastructure concentration (data centers) is divorced from distributed capability-building, indicating shallow engagement outside tech hubs.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI adoption pressure on Richmond's young workforce suggests capability is concentrating in metro areas with existing talent pipelines, deepening the metro-rural divide as workforce demands cluster geographically.

signals.title: Israeli AI maritime tech company joins Virginia Beach incubator - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: An Israeli maritime AI firm joining Virginia Beach's incubator demonstrates specialized deep capability forming in Hampton Roads' defense/maritime niche, reinforcing sector-specific excellence clusters rather than distributed fluency.

signals.title: Trump pushes data centers. That puts him in opposition to many of his supporters.
signals.signal_reading: Rural Republican opposition to data centers reveals infrastructure concentration without local capability-building or benefit-sharing, signaling neither depth nor distribution in Virginia's historically underserved regions.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: UVA students helping businesses explore AI represents university-mediated knowledge transfer that could distribute capability beyond metro hubs if scaled, though current impact remains concentrated in university-adjacent communities.
